purpose: Conditional interface opportunity with complete finite drain; no native timing, novelty or deployment claim.

origin.negative_result: M0 accepted-read DS return priority removes P/PN difference, but actual fixed MIG cannot move a newly accepted PTE before accepted payload reads.
source_facts: Legal PTW start can precede local and aggregated DS AR VALID.
Existing offers and accepted obligations are irreversible at this selector.
Normal source-ready / cold-destination and a different DMA source read blocked at its eventual write by V W ownership are individually sourced.
4 KiB jobs and 512-beat source capacity are preserved; one AXI burst is at most 256 beats.
conditional_not_observed: The candidate ticket reaches the gate before L first offer.
The public selector history can be identical in the cold and hot initial states.
The chosen PTW processing intervals and relative job readiness occur together.
Serial response/data service law and every numerical duration below.

time_convention: Integer boundaries, service intervals [start,end), events at end retire before new selection. At most one AR is selected per boundary. AR admission preserves FIFO read order. If P1 wins at t, L can first be admitted at t+1. No retroactive cancellation. No new request can be served ahead of an already active nonpreemptive transaction.

work.mapping: Sv39 stage 1, G Bare, three PTE reads for the cold V destination; hot case has an already cached valid destination translation.
work.source_initial_suffix_state: V has all 512 source beats legally retained; A has its first 256 source beats retained. L is A's second 256-beat read, translation valid. V owns the first write burst and is waiting for its destination translation. A's write may not pass that owner. No held or accepted L exists in the positive case.

common_prefix.meaning: An accounted common causal prefix, not an observed trace. Add P0 to suffix completion times. An early-prepare control may change this prefix and must be charged from the same earlier task start.

work.payload_memory: Original two 4096-byte full buffers; no capacity reduction or extra payload storage. Mapping/physical retention is unchanged.
work.termination: Both jobs successful, all source R beats, four W bursts and four B responses accounted, all queues/tickets empty. No STOP A or truncation.

service_law.shared_resource: One serial memory data resource for all modeled R and W work. A read burst, once started, is nonpreemptive. Each beat costs one model time unit. This does not assert the actual MIG has this service timing.
service_law.A_write_ready: L_R_complete, but initial V W owner must retire first
service_law.write_order_meaning: Ordinary fixed RR continuation after the initially owned V0, used identically by all policies. Each write has its own 256-beat AW/W and B. Do not merge into illegal 512-beat bursts. Prefix/baseline changes may not silently give A an earlier owner than allowed.
service_law.write_scheduling: At each service boundary, retain any active transaction; then service oldest accepted read, else next ready write in the fixed owner sequence. A write is not published before its translation/data/owner predicates. If a ready write exists while no accepted read is available, it may run: do not idle it just to privilege the construction.
service_law.B_overlap: B is an AXI control response, retires exactly b_response after that write burst's WLAST, can overlap later data service; quiet is max of every B, R, write, offer and ticket retirement.
service_law.registration: The illustrative values already include the explicitly modeled PTW/DS/TC gaps; no unlisted native pipeline latency is inferred.

interface.event: An actual accepted PTW start sends a one-shot dependency intent before the gate's first L offer. This is an observation, not a translation success or memory access permission.
interface.identity: Mark the first physical PTE AR of this walk. Carry one matching marker through the real seven-way DS selection and every relevant spill stage to the shared selector. Never consume the ticket on an unrelated aggregate DS request.
interface.action: While a valid bounded ticket is pending and there is no old held offer, suppress only a new non-DS payload first offer. Continue all original DS/R/W/B and committed traffic. Release after the tagged P1 is accepted into the selector output spill, so a subsequent L cannot precede it. P2/P3 get only ordinary current-VALID priority; no whole-walk reservation.
interface.timeout: At H elapsed model units reopen payload admission if no tagged acceptance occurred. Timeout never cancels a held target or payload. If the hint arrives after L first offer, keep L and record missed_window.
interface.fairness: After one ticket episode, require one available non-DS acceptance before another ticket may close its gate; use ordinary DS-first/F4 for selection. Pending DS can receive up to four consecutive selector acceptances, then available non-DS gets a turn. Downstream readiness is an explicit liveness assumption, not a wall-clock guarantee.

state_cost.marker_pipeline_bits: N_tag, number of actual marker-holding entries/stages, unknown
state_cost.escape_and_epoch: May share the three-state gate/ordinary F4 state only if proved; otherwise count additional bits. No free epoch matching across reset or overlapping walks.
state_cost.CPU_cost: No per-transfer CPU action in the proposed hardware control; integration/setup and comparison-control CPU costs are unknown, not zero.

ordinary: current legal aggregate DS AR head and non-DS AR heads
existing shared-selector held/acceptance history and downstream ready
public W validity and owner history available at the declared implementation boundary
public AR fields/history and any explicitly charged response counters
not_granted_to_ordinary: private PTW accepted-start before a DS head is visible
observation.paired_state_scope: Identical only for declared selector-observable history up to time 0, and until P1 appears at d in cold. In both states no public WVALID is available at time 0. This is not a claim of identical CPU/software/full-system history, nor proof of a native indistinguishable prefix.

policies.rule: Existing-interface current-VALID DS-first/F4. L offered at time 0 if no DS head exists. Preserve held/accepted FIFO obligations.
The interface rule above plus exactly O_CURRENT. Cold timely intent holds L until tagged P1 acceptance; hot has no intent and does not delay L.

A single fixed initial guard G begins when L first becomes eligible. During [0,G), withhold L but accept DS normally. From G onward use O_CURRENT. Same G across cold/hot and all cases; no per-state chosen G. Prior public history is identical in the paired case.

Ordinary if/else gating using the same paid intent, marker, timeout and fairness. Must be event-for-event equal to M_TICKET. This excludes a distinct scheduling-algorithm claim, not the value or prior publication status of the interface.

policies.classification: conditional ordinary prepare control from the full earlier start
policies.rule: Allow legal destination preparation before/during the 768-beat source prefix if an actual existing interface permits it. An optimistic executable full-start schedule is P1, V source256, P2, V source256, P3, A source256; then A final256 and all four writes. All PTE gaps and final translation tail fit in the intervening 256-beat source bursts for the main parameters. This adds the same 3 PTE beats to prefix service and eliminates suffix walk stalls.
policies.conditions: Requires the actual legal prepare interface, original permissions/lifetime, job address knowledge and enough overlap. CPU/extra-descriptor/lookup/serialization costs must be added. If this schedule is already legal at comparable cost, the positive interface opportunity is absent in that domain. Do not assert those conditions are false because the actual current source has not been checked.

policies.classification: strong ordinary paid post-translation read splitter or adapted legalizer
policies.rule: Keep the original 4096-byte parent, mapping and fullbuffer qualification. Split only L=256 beats into two 128-beat physical reads. Issue first at t=0. Do not offer second until the first RLAST; at that boundary give any visible DS head ordinary priority, then offer second. Preserve full parent attributes, error aggregation and final RLAST; no extra write splitting in this particular paid implementation.
policies.interface_status: Not a native read-only128 runtime switch: current reg64 ties src/dst length limits to zero and CONF.deburst affects both. An explicit backend adaptation needs independent src limit and decouple_rw=1; alternatively a paid post-TL splitter needs header/phase/return joining. Native absence is not evidence of high cost.
policies.cost: a_split is additional EXPOSED delay for the extra split boundary, not automatically one cycle per added AR. In the model charge it as a serial setup interval immediately after the first 128-beat R completes and before the next data transaction. Physically hidden extra-AR overhead gives a_split=0; actual area/logic/routing/CPU remain unknown.
policies.comparison: For main parameters quiet=1290+a_split versus M_TICKET=1292. Thus split wins for a_split<2, ties for 2, candidate wins for >2. Hot split quiet=1282+a_split versus M_TICKET=1282. a_split=0 reproduces or improves the whole paired service vector with one additional AR; do not claim the early interface is necessary for completion improvement.
policies.implementation_requirement: Include this executable paced two-piece control in the first model run. One piece at a time is an ordinary chosen policy, not a forced restriction on other controls. Existing spare metadata may be reused legally, with actual cost unproven.

policies.classification: ordinary legal decomposition, including existing all-channel single-beat deburst
policies.rule: Preserve the entire parent copy, attributes, errors, permissions and all B joins. Let chunk sizes be 1,16,64,128,256 where an implementable child controller is explicitly charged; only chunk=1 is the cited existing stock all-channel deburst. Permit voluntary one-read-outstanding pacing and DS-first at each chunk boundary, and permit more credits if beneficial. Do not compare a free arbitrary read-only segmentation knob to stock.
policies.accounting: For stock full single-beat deburst, payload AR=1024 and AW=B=1024, plus three PTE AR in cold. Unsplit totals are payload AR=4 and AW=B=4. Extra controller/address/B traffic and possible loss of overlap are separate costs. A zero-overhead segmentation lower-cost construction can reach shared service work plus B latency (2053 full units), so it can beat M_TICKET's 2060 illustrative full units; report this instead of manufacturing a win. If modeled or measured segmentation exposes >7 extra critical-path units over that 2053 construction, M_TICKET becomes faster on this example; CPU/area tradeoffs remain separate.
policies.execution_scope: Implement at least stock chunk=1 or explicitly label the 2053 schedule as an optimistic ordinary service construction; do not call unimplemented cost parameter sweeps measured results.

derived_scope.main_formula: For L long enough to cover tau1 and no old obligations, positive candidate reduction = tau1-d (here 8-2=6); P1 response and first-L publication are one unit each as explicitly modeled. General formula must retain P1 service/publication delay and max() if L is short.
derived_scope.fixed_guard_tradeoff: G=2 reproduces the main cold completion but delays paired hot completion by 2; G=0 matches hot but loses 6 in cold. This is an information/cost tradeoff, not a claim that candidate dominates every fixed-G completion vector.
derived_scope.same_interface_equivalence: Required and accepted, not a failure of the interface study.
derived_scope.prepare_or_segment_counterexample: At zero additional cost the legal optimistic early-prepare/full-deburst construction finishes at 2053 full units versus M_TICKET at 2060. Therefore this document cannot establish universal net benefit or choose a paper contribution. It specifies a useful candidate under the concrete cost/interface domains stated above.
derived_scope.split_counterexample: O_SPLIT_128_PACED at a_split=0 finishes cold two units earlier than M_TICKET and matches hot, with one extra AR. The strongest surviving proposed benefit is avoiding split/reassembly/extra-AR cost when that cost exceeds d or is a meaningful resource objective. That domain is conditional, not a demonstrated native cost advantage.

assertions: Every main and adjacent run preserves exact useful bytes and completes both jobs, all R/W/B and final drain.
No read burst exceeds 256 beats; unsegmented full copy remains two read/two write bursts per job.
No P2 before P1 completion+tau1; no P3 before P2 completion+tau2; no cold V AW before P3 completion+tau_final.
No A write passes initially owned V0; fixed W owner continuation is identical across compared strategies.
No accepted or held L is withdrawn, no accepted FIFO read is promoted, and candidate never gates original W/B/R obligations.
Tagged P1, not any DS head, discharges the ticket.
M_TICKET and O_SAME_TICKET have identical event traces.
Cold/hot declared public histories before decision are equal; private hidden state is exposed only through the paid candidate interface.
Every guard is one cross-state program; never merge per-case winners into one control.
All five frozen numerical cases satisfy the expected results or report a specification/implementation error without tuning parameters to restore a win.
Timeout/cancel/held/error are protocol cases, not automatically successful performance records.
Physical area, Fmax, native source prefix reachability and actual comparison costs remain null/unknown until actual evidence exists.

O_SPLIT_128_PACED a_split=0 has the frozen expected full completion and one extra AR, and all its original parent/error/RLAST obligations remain represented; stock deburst and paid read-only split are not conflated.
failure_protocol: Preserve failed outputs. Correct only a concrete protocol, arithmetic or implementation error; record the amendment before rerun. Do not search parameters after seeing holdout results.
not_authorized_by_this_spec: new mechanism novelty claim from the timing example alone

spec_amendments.reason: Root identified a stronger legal ordinary control: paced 2x128 splitting hides both d and tau1. Added before any model execution; no parameter tuning or result-driven revision.
